claim: Across twelve MCP servers, the SDK's major version decided which protocol era each spoke, with no exceptions

baseline.source: sqlite-mcp on Python SDK 2.2.0, probed the same way
baseline.note: the control: a server on an SDK that implements the revision answers discover

scale: 12 servers at their latest published versions, each probed down both negotiation paths on separate stdio connections, all on one build of the probe. Reference: everything, filesystem, memory (TypeScript sdk 1.30.0); fetch, time, git (Python mcp 1.30.0). Vendors: Playwright (Microsoft, TypeScript v1 bundled in playwright-core), dbt-mcp (dbt Labs, Python mcp 1.26.0), Context7 (Upstash, TypeScript server 2.0.0), MotherDuck (Python mcp 2.2.0), AWS Documentation (AWS Labs, Python mcp 2.2.0). Control: sqlite-mcp.
code_path: model-free; stdio only; local subprocesses via npx and uvx, no credentials, no tool calls, no hosted endpoints
surprise: TypeScript v2 is not a new major version of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. It shipped on 2026-07-27 as new packages, @modelcontextprotocol/server, /client and /node, so a project that keeps bumping the package it already depends on stays on the old protocol indefinitely. Separately, the two v1 SDKs refuse an unknown method differently: TypeScript with -32601 Method not found, Python with -32602 Invalid request parameters. A client that falls back to the handshake only on -32601 would fail against every Python v1 server here.
corrections: An earlier version of this card, from the same morning, covered only the six reference servers and said the TypeScript SDK's newest release predated the revision. That was true only of the old @modelcontextprotocol/sdk package name.
It also said the Python v1 error's code and message disagreed. They don't: a summary script had truncated 'Invalid request parameters' to 'Invalid request'.
expires: as servers migrate to v2 SDKs; re-run before quoting
